learningObjective: Explain why row-max subtraction is required for a numerically stable softmax and what happens when it is omitted.

canonicalClaims.claim: softmax(x) = softmax(x - c) for any constant c; choosing c = max_j x_j clamps every exponent to (0, 1] and prevents overflow while preserving the exact softmax result.
conditions: The reduction accumulates in sufficient precision (typically FP32).
nonImplications: Does not eliminate all rounding differences from summation order.
Does not remove the need for tiling / online algorithms on very long rows.

misconceptions.claim: Naive softmax and safe softmax differ only on integer hardware.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FP hardware also has finite exponent range; exp(90) overflows in FP32 and produces NaN in the ratio.

misconceptions.claim: IEEE-754 inf/inf cancellation produces the correct softmax without max subtraction.
misconceptions.whyWrong: inf / inf is NaN, not a ratio; overflow poisons the whole vector.

misconceptions.claim: Max subtraction shifts softmax outputs by an additive offset absorbed downstream.
misconceptions.whyWrong: In exact arithmetic softmax(x - c) equals softmax(x); no shift is introduced.

implementationFacts: FP16 exp overflows around x ≈ 11; BF16 around x ≈ 88 (same as FP32).
Attention logits (Q@K^T / sqrt(d)) can be well over FP16 overflow range for typical d and unnormalized weights.
performanceScenarios: Long-sequence attention requires online (tiled) softmax that maintains a running max and running denominator (FlashAttention).
